title: Crimble Mill’s housing plans must balance heritage rescue with the cost to local families
body:
Crimble Mill’s detailed scheme is 214 homes: 33 apartments in the mill, 31 houses in the existing complex and 150 houses on neighbouring greenfield land. The broader 250-home allocation is not a second development or the approved detailed count.

Urban Green names Redwaters (Crimble) Ltd and Prescot Business Park Ltd as clients. Committee approval was reported in August 2023, but this review did not retrieve the executed legal agreement and formal notice completing the approval process.

Historic England identifies the principal mill complex as Grade II* listed. The restoration’s timing matters as much as the housing total: the recommended obligations tie public benefits to development phasing.

The affordability and infrastructure provisions below are recommendations, rather than verified final payments or funded service expansions. In particular, a mixed-purpose contribution must not be reported as wholly dedicated to affordable housing.

No verified site-specific adverse builder finding was established. The public accountability questions are whether the restoration obligations are enforceable, which benefits the eventual payment buys, and when those benefits reach residents.

Location: Crimble Lane, Heywood

Planning stage: Committee approval reported August 2023; signed deed and formal decision notice not verified

Homes: 214 detailed proposal: 33 mill apartments, 31 complex houses and 150 greenfield houses; distinct from 250 allocation

Let or for sale: No on-site affordable homes in committee viability assessment; final tenure/household prices unverified

Land: Mixed: existing mill/brownfield fabric and neighbouring greenfield land

Final planning agreement: Committee approval was reported in August 2023, subject to further procedural steps and agreement. The complete signed deed, formal notice and variations were not verified. The report recommends restoration/phasing obligations, a viability reappraisal if not started within 18 months, school land and a traffic regulation order.

Exact rents / prices: No exact final apartment/house asking prices, rental offer or household charges established from the reviewed records.

Affordable breakdown: The committee material supports no on-site affordable provision on viability grounds. Recommended £803,193 is for off-site affordable housing AND/OR open space and formal sport: it must not all be labelled an affordable-housing payment. Final allocation and signed terms are unverified.

Funded school capacity: Land beside All Souls is recommended for future expansion. A land transfer is not a funded expansion; a budget, additional places and opening date are not established.

Funded healthcare capacity: No site-specific funded NHS expansion, additional staffed appointment capacity or delivery date was established from the accessible council/government records reviewed. Proximity to a surgery is not a capacity assessment.

Funded transport capacity: A Crimble Lane traffic regulation order is among proposed obligations. Its final funding/delivery and additional bus-service capacity were not established.

The outstanding details identified above are not yet available to Rochdale Daily. This article will be updated when the information becomes available.

Research checked 14 October 2026. Advertised prices are snapshots, not achieved sale prices.

Read the borough-wide housing investigation and the other developments: https://rochdaledaily.co.uk/articles/rochdale-housing-developments-affordability-schools-gp-transport.html
